what: Phase 2 steering attempt 5 — the predicted oscillation happened; criterion 2b (the repair) PASSED
verdict: FAIL — 6 of 8. 2a (heading error trends to zero) and 3 (no saturated oscillation) both fail.
headline: The oscillation registered in §4 of the predeclaration BEFORE dispatch is exactly what happened. That prediction coming true is the strongest evidence in this run.
criterion_2_repair_vindicated: 2b PASSED: |cross_track| peaked at 0.0864 m (d3) then decreased across TWO consecutive decisions (0.0651, 0.0084). The structural argument in the predeclaration — that cross-track cannot decrease until heading error crosses zero, and attempt 4's 1.00 m bound stopped it exactly at that crossing — is confirmed. The repair was correct and it was not a free pass: 2a and 3 still failed.

deviation_from_predeclaration.what: corridor recentred on the live position and reduced from 7.0x7.0 m to 6.0x6.0 m
deviation_from_predeclaration.why: the mower sat 1.159 m from the predeclared centre (5.98,-5.24), outside the 0.95 m placement tolerance, and its clearance in the predeclared corridor was 2.5253 m against the required 2.55 m — short by 24.7 mm. Recentring the 7x7 on the live position satisfied clearance but left only 0.039 m of corner margin against the yard boundary (yard clearance 4.9886 m vs corner reach 4.9497 m). The 6x6 gives 3.000 m of start clearance (>= the required 2.55) and 0.746 m of corner margin.
deviation_from_predeclaration.what_did_NOT_change: every criterion, the distance budget (max_distance_m 1.75), duration_ms 8000, max_cross_track_m 0.30, angular cap 120, linear 400, the 8 deg route offset. Section 5 of the predeclaration already lists 6x6 as satisfying the requirement.
deviation_from_predeclaration.flagged: stated to the operator before dispatch, not applied silently

3_no_saturated_oscillation.evidence: angular [0, -110, -120, -111, 0, 120, 120]: saturated -120 at d2 then saturated +120 at d5 and d6 -- a reversal between saturated commands of opposite sign

5_hard_abort_never_fires.evidence: stopped on the 8000 ms window, not the 0.30 m cross-track abort; max |cross| 0.0864 m

the_mechanism.finding: ACTUATION LAG EXCEEDS THE CONTROL PERIOD, measured directly for the first time.
evidence: interval 4->5: commanded angular was ZERO and the mower still rotated +7.861 deg/s -- nearly the fastest rate in the run
interval 5->6: commanded angular was +120, the REVERSING direction, and the mower still rotated +5.402 deg/s the SAME way
the rate decayed +7.593 (cmd -111) -> +7.861 (cmd 0) -> +5.402 (cmd +120) and never reversed inside the ~8 s window
the_mechanism.consequence: the rotational time constant is comparable to or larger than the ~1 Hz decision period, so a proportional-only loop carries roughly a full period of dead time. Oscillation is then structural, not a gain-tuning error.
the_mechanism.do_not: do NOT respond by lowering angular_speed_per_heading_degree. A gain change cannot fix dead time that exceeds the sample period; it only changes the amplitude of the same hunt.

sign_is_still_correct: The second-half divergence is OSCILLATION about the setpoint, NOT sign inversion. The error converged cleanly first (+9.176 -> +13.151 -> +9.215 -> +0.133), crossing zero, then overshot. An inverted sign diverges monotonically from the first decision, as the 2026-08-24 run did (46.64 -> 48.25 -> 77.40). Do NOT invoke the run-1 'stop and re-derive the sign' rule here.
